name: Plan Matrix
job: Lay out a role plan as duties against time marks, every cell a proposal the reader can edit, with how they would know it is working at each mark.

anatomy.role: Small, secondary: where the rows come from and that every cell is a proposal
Optional, small, secondary: one caveat that changes how to read the plan
Duty column semibold (28%), one column per horizon; body 0.9375rem; hairline rows
By day N, one per horizon, from data (any count, any values)
One cell per horizon: a mono label and one sentence on how the reader would know it is working
Below 600px each row stacks: the duty, then each mark with its horizon as a label

states.name: Three horizons
states.note: The default for a six-month seat.

states.name: Twelve-month engagement
states.note: Horizons are data, so a longer engagement needs no template change.

states.name: One duty
states.note: A short plan still reads as a matrix.

use_when: A page proposes what someone will do by when, and the reader should be able to edit it.
The rows come from the reader’s own document (a job page, an RFP, a statement of work).
avoid_when: A schedule with dependencies or dates; use a timeline.
More than five horizons; the columns stop reading on a laptop.

data.note: Day marks, one column each, for example 30, 90, 180.
Each row: the duty, then one cell per horizon.
Where the rows come from; one caveat.

access: A real `<table>` with `<th>` column headers; screen readers read each cell with its horizon.
On phones the header row hides and each mark carries its horizon as visible text (`data-label`), so nothing depends on position.
Static: no interaction, nothing hidden, prints whole.
gates: `scripts/kit_primitive_sync.py --check`: every page that marks this block carries it unchanged.
`scripts/page_gate.py`, `scripts/token_source_gate.py`, and the Impeccable detector at 0 findings.
